item.title: Introducing: AutoRange Pools
item.dc:creator: Tiago Hansen
item.content:encoded:
Concentrated liquidity is one of DeFi’s most powerful mechanisms. It can multiply capital efficiency by up to 4000x compared to a standard AMM, which means more fees per dollar deployed for anyone who can keep a position in range.

The catch is that keeping a position in range takes work. Active monitoring, periodic rebalancing, decisions about where the market is heading. That overhead is why, five years after concentrated liquidity was introduced, most of the efficiency is still captured by professional operators, not passive LPs.

Why concentrated liquidity is hard for most LPs

Three structural problems get in the way.

The first is range management. A position only earns fees while the price stays inside its range. When the market moves outside, the position ends up holding only one of the two tokens and stops generating yield. Bringing it back in line means withdrawing, choosing a new range, and redepositing. That costs gas, costs attention, and requires a view on where the market is heading. A meaningful share of retail concentrated liquidity LPs end up underwater because the work to stay in range is more than they signed up for.

The second is NFT fragmentation. Each standard CL position is a unique ERC-721 with its own range and accounting. Two LPs in the same pool with overlapping ranges still hold different tokens that cannot be combined. NFTs are clumsy as collateral, complicate incentive distribution, and break every downstream integration that expects a standard fungible token.

The third is JIT attacks. Just-in-time bots watch the mempool for large incoming trades, insert a concentrated position right before the swap executes, collect the fee it generates, and withdraw in the same transaction. Passive LPs provide the underlying liquidity, but the bot extracts the fee income they showed up to earn. Research found bots deploying up to 269 times the trade volume to execute this, meaning a small set of actors is systematically extracting fees from the broader pool.

Why active liquidity managers are only a partial fix

The market response to these problems has been third-party Active Liquidity Managers (ALMs), protocols that hold the underlying CL positions on the user’s behalf and rebalance them through external keepers. The approach works, but it stacks a new set of trade-offs on top of the original problem.

ALMs typically rely on off-chain keepers to monitor prices and trigger rebalances. That introduces an external system the LP has to trust to stay online, honest, and well-funded. Most ALMs charge a management fee on top of swap fees, which eats into what is already a thin-margin position.

Strategies are often opaque, with closed-source rebalancing logic and limited visibility into when and why a position moves. The trust assumption compounds: the LP now relies on the underlying DEX, the ALM contracts, and the keeper infrastructure behind them.

For passive LPs and DAO treasuries, that is a lot of moving parts to evaluate before depositing.

How AutoRange Pools work

The experience for an LP is straightforward: deposit a pair of tokens, and the pool handles the rest. The range adjusts on its own as the market moves. No withdrawals, reconfigurations, or monitoring required.

Here is how that works.

When the pool is created, it is set up with a price range and a target at its center. Think of the range as a window. Trades happen inside that window, and the pool earns fees on every swap.

If the market moves far enough in one direction, the window starts following it. There is a threshold, called the margin, that determines how far the price has to drift before the range begins to move. Once that threshold is crossed, the range shifts gradually in the same direction, at a steady pace. The shift is smooth rather than abrupt, and the range always catches up without overshooting.

The entire process runs from the pool’s own trade history, with no oracle feeding prices in from outside, no keeper watching for trigger conditions, and no external account sending update transactions. The pool reads where it has been and adjusts accordingly.

Because all LPs in the same pool share the same range, they all hold the same LP token, and that token is a standard ERC-20, the same format as any other DeFi token. This means it can be deposited as collateral, moved through a governance vote, or included in any incentive program without special handling.

Who AutoRange Pools are for

DAOs and Treasuries

DAOs and treasuries can provide deep liquidity for a native token without delegating control to a liquidity manager or third-party keeper.

The pool manages its own range, so capital stays within the treasury rather than locked inside an external strategy. That autonomy extends to the LP positions themselves, which can participate in governance votes and incentive programs without any special infrastructure.

Passive LPs

Passive LPs get the capital efficiency of concentrated liquidity without the overhead that usually comes with it. The range adjusts automatically as the market moves, so fees keep accruing without any action needed to stay in range. Deposit the pair and let it earn from swaps.

Protocols

For protocols, AutoRange Pools provide a concentrated liquidity primitive that composes with the rest of DeFi. Positions are standard ERC-20 tokens, so they work as collateral in lending markets, move through governance systems, and plug into incentive programs with no custom handling.

The pool is also oracle-free, meaning price comes entirely from its own trading activity, which removes an external dependency from the integration stack and eliminates the manipulation surface that oracle-dependent protocols carry.

Building on reCLAMM

AutoRange Pools shipped as reCLAMM first. Before the rename, the codebase went through two independent audits, Cantina and Certora, alongside AI-assisted analysis from Nethermind, Octane, and Failsafe.

  • Cantina: https://github.com/balancer/reclamm/blob/reclamm-2.1/audits/cantina/2026-04-13.pdf
  • Certora: https://github.com/balancer/reclamm/blob/reclamm-2.1/audits/certora/2026-04-23.pdf

Both firms had previously audited Balancer V3 and returned for AutoRange Pools, coming in with direct familiarity with the underlying infrastructure rather than starting from scratch.

Live at launch

Neverland is running an AutoRange Pools from day one. Both pools were parameter-tuned ahead of deployment using the Balancer simulator, an internal tool that models how an AutoRange Pool behaves under different market conditions before going live. We use it to test the margin, shift rate, and price range against historical data for the specific pair being deployed.

If you are evaluating AutoRange Pools for a token or pair, our team can run a simulation and walk you through the report. Reach out to the Balancer team.

Introducing: AutoRange Pools was originally published in Balancer Protocol on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: What 961 Token Launches Taught Us About LBP Configuration
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Frequently, LBP configurations are chosen by gut feeling. Teams copy what the last project did, tweak a number or two, and hope for the best. There’s rarely a data-backed reason behind any of it.

We wanted to change that, and provide teams a way to test their LBP parameters before actually launching the pool. That’s why we, in partnership with NEO Empresarial, analyzed 961 Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools deployed across Ethereum, Polygon, and Arbitrum, spanning every swap, liquidity event, and bot transaction from 2021 through 2024. The goal was to figure out which parameters actually affect launch outcomes, and which ones are just noise.

How We Built the Dataset

All onchain data was sourced from @dune, querying Balancer V1 and V2 pool contracts across Ethereum, Polygon, and Arbitrum. The raw extraction returned over 2,400 rows, but that included noise: configuration updates, pool pauses, resets, and test deployments that never ran a real sale. To isolate actual launches, we filtered out any pool with a duration under 12 hours and kept only the earliest valid event per pool address. That brought the dataset down to 961 unique launches.

Success Isn’t Predictable, But Failure Is

The first thing we tried was building a model to predict which configurations would produce successful launches. It didn’t work.

We tested every standard prediction model against the data. The best one explained about 5% of what makes a launch successful. To put that in perspective, that’s like trying to predict whether a restaurant succeeds by only looking at the kitchen layout. The layout matters, but the food, the service, the location, and the reviews matter a lot more. Same thing here. Configuration is one input. Marketing, community strength, narrative timing, and project quality make up the other 95%.

But when we flipped the question and asked “which configurations are basically guaranteed to fail?”, the data lit up. Our model correctly identified launches headed for heavy sell-offs about 3 out of 4 times, scoring 0.76 out of 1.0 on the AUC metric, which is the standard used by financial institutions to validate whether a risk model is reliable enough for real decision-making. We couldn’t predict winners, but we could spot the losers before they even started.

A perfect configuration won’t save a weak project from a bad launch, but a bad configuration will sink a strong one.

Here’s what we analyzed. Each LBP was broken down into these configurable parameters:

The question then became: what configurations are teams using, and do any of them reliably produce better outcomes?

What Most Teams Actually Do

Before getting into what the results show, here’s what teams are doing in practice.

The average LBP in our dataset ran for about 88 hours (roughly 3.5 days). Starting weights were concentrated between 90% and 99% for the project token, showing near-universal agreement on starting high. Most teams also avoided launching on weekends, likely to maximize participation during regular trading hours.

Where strategies diverged was on ending weights. The data showed two clear camps: one group went for a full flip (ending near 10–20% project weight), and another aimed for a soft landing at 50/50, setting the pool up to transition directly into a standard trading pair.

The rate of weight change (slope) stayed consistently low, averaging around 0.01 per hour. Even as teams chose different durations and end weights, they tended to keep the shift gradual.

But none of these individual choices correlated strongly with success on their own. Our correlation matrix showed near-zero coefficients across the board. There’s no single “magic number” for any parameter. The data instead pointed to specific combinations and thresholds that matter, which we break down below.

Weight Slope: The Parameter That Kills Launches

While most parameters showed weak individual effects, one stood out clearly above the rest.

Weight slope is how fast the token weights change per hour during the sale. Out of everything we tested, the data shows it’s the only parameter that can single-handedly cause a launch to fail.

Think of it like a faucet. Below 0.6, the price drains slowly enough that buyers can keep up. Above 0.6, the faucet is fully open and the pool is dumping tokens faster than anyone can absorb them. It doesn’t matter how much demand you have. The math overwhelms the market.

The data shows a sharp inflection point at 0.6. Above that threshold, the probability of excessive dump pressure spikes. Keeping slope below 0.6 appears to be the single most important configuration decision a team can make.

The Duration Sweet Spot

Duration matters, but not in the way most teams assume. The common instinct is that longer launches are safer because they give more people time to participate. The data says otherwise.

Bot activity follows a U-curve. Too short and too long are both bad, but for different reasons.

Pools under 24 hours don’t give real people enough time to find the sale, read up on the project, and decide to buy. The data showed these short pools also suffered from capital inefficiency, since there simply wasn’t enough time for meaningful trading volume to develop. Pools over 72 hours turn into a slow, predictable price drop that bots can feed on for days. Think of it like leaving your front door open overnight versus locking up after a few hours. The longer the window stays open, the more uninvited guests walk in.

The numbers back it up. Medium-duration pools (24 to 72 hours) saw bot activity around 10.4%. Pools under 24 hours came in at 11.8%. But pools over 72 hours jumped to 16.8%, over 60% more bot activity than the middle range.

On the capital efficiency side, risk drops steadily as duration increases from 12 hours, then flattens around the 72-hour mark. Going beyond three days added no measurable safety benefit in our dataset while increasing bot exposure.

The data suggests an optimal window of 48 to 72 hours. Long enough for genuine price discovery, short enough to avoid becoming a target.

The Parameters That Matter Less

Two of the most debated LBP parameters, starting weight ratios and swap fees, turned out to be statistically irrelevant to launch outcomes in our analysis.

We tested the hypothesis that starting at a more extreme ratio (say 95/5 versus 80/20) provides meaningful protection against price crashes. The correlation with price retention came back at 0.049. The correlation with dump pressure was -0.098. Both are effectively zero. A token launching at 50/50 is just as likely to crash as one launching at 90/10 if the underlying demand isn’t there.

Swap fees showed the same flatness across the entire range, with less than 5% variance in risk outcomes. Whether you set fees at 1% or 3%, the data showed no meaningful change to the safety profile of the pool.

The research suggests these are preference parameters, not safety parameters. Teams can set them based on revenue or marketing goals. According to our analysis, they don’t appear to significantly affect launch outcomes either way.

What Healthy Launches Actually Look Like

To validate the model, we ran a forensic comparison between failed LBPs (high bot sniping, heavy dumps, severe price collapse) and the healthiest pools in the dataset.

Two patterns stood out. Healthy pools had an average starting weight of around 94%, while dumped pools averaged closer to 87%. A dominant initial project weight creates a high-price buffer that absorbs early volatility. Lower starting weights leave the pool exposed to immediate selling pressure the liquidity curve can’t dampen.

Sniped pools also ran significantly longer, averaging around 100 hours compared to 87 hours for healthy pools. Duration didn’t protect them. It gave sophisticated actors more time to extract value.

Final Thoughts

Configuration is a defense layer, not a growth lever. It won’t make a weak project succeed, but it will stop a strong project from failing mechanically. LBPs put projects in full control of that configuration, with pricing and execution happening onchain where anyone can verify. Now there’s data to back those decisions.

This research helps teams back up their choices. Which parameters carry weight, which ones are cosmetic, where the risk thresholds are, and what the healthiest launches in the dataset had in common.

For teams that want to dig into the methodology, see how the scoring model was built, or explore the full correlation and failure analysis, the full report is available.

If you’re planning a launch, stress-test your configuration before committing a single token. The LBP Simulator lets you model demand scenarios, visualize price curves, and pressure-test your parameters against real data.

Whether you’re ready to launch or still figuring out your approach, reach out to our team. We are happy to help with configuration, strategy, or just answering questions.

What 961 Token Launches Taught Us About LBP Configuration was originally published in Balancer Protocol on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Balancer x Certora: Future-Proofing Protocol Security
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Certora Re-Audit + New Security Guardrails: Building Preventive Security Into V3

Following the November 3rd exploit targeting Composable Stable Pools on V2, Balancer took decisive action. While V3 remained completely unaffected, we recognized an opportunity to strengthen our security posture even further. Rather than waiting for threats to emerge, we decided to build future-proofing protocol security on V3.

The Preventive Security Mindset

The CSP exploit revealed that attack vector had existed for over four years before anyone discovered it. Similar exploits hit other protocols after our incident, yet the pattern remained invisible to the industry. This reality forced us to rethink our entire approach.

Traditional security operates reactively: find vulnerabilities, patch them, move on. But what about the vulnerabilities we don’t know exist yet? What about attack vectors that won’t be discovered for another four year?

Our answer to that problem is to eliminate entire categories of potential exploits by constraining protocols to only legitimate use cases. If an operation has no valid use case to exist, it shouldn’t be possible at all.

V3’s Structural Advantages

V3’s architecture already embodies this philosophy. The vault-centric approach centralizes token balances, fees, BPT management into a single, heavily audited system. With this and other design choices, V3 eliminates multiple attack surfaces that could be exploited by malicious actors, including the specific rounding vulnerability that enabled the November 3rd exploit. The proof is in the results: zero V3 pools were affected by the incident.

But we didn’t stop there.

Comprehensive Re-Audit with Certora

In partnership with Certora, we conducted an extensive re-audit of many V3 contracts. The goal was to identify and eliminate any possible attack vector before it could be discovered by bad actors.

The Certora team found no vulnerabilities across the audited V3 contracts, highlighting the power of V3’s simplified architecture. By moving complexity away from individual pools and into the vault, we’ve created a system that’s more secure by design.

For more details regarding the methodology and results, please read Certora’s full report on the security reassessment.

New Security Guardrails: Constraining to Legitimate Use

Beyond the clean audit, we implemented additional security guardrails across both Weighted and Stable pools, to restrict protocol activity to valid use cases.

Weighted Pool Guardrails

On weighted pools, we added two preventive guardrails that directly eliminate malicious use cases:

  • Minimum Token Balance Limits: We’ve implemented minimum token balances that are effective across the entire range of token decimals. Since reaching very low balances generally requires very large trades, this effectively limits the maximum trade size, and restricts pool operations to an economically meaningful range.
  • Enhanced Balance Rounding: Originally, liquidity operations in the Vault that require specific rounding pass the required rounding direction to the pools. In V3, the pool math itself always rounds correctly. In particular, the amountIn rounding for ExactOut swaps is now correct, addressing the issue present in V2. On top of this, we also round up the tokenIn balance during calculations, further pushing the already correct rounding in a safer direction.

Stable Pool Guardrails

We also added one new guardrail to V3 stable pools:

  • Maximum Imbalance Ratio: Stable pools now enforce a maximum 10,000:1 ratio between the highest and lowest token balances. While stable pools are designed to maintain near 1:1 balance, this generous ceiling still blocks the extreme imbalances that characterize known attack patterns. The main idea is to restrict Stable pools to an operating range that is economically meaningful. There’s no valid use case for operating at such extreme imbalances, so we’re forbidding it entirely.

Flash Swaps

One critical realization shaped our approach: flash swaps are not flash loans. While both allow temporary access to assets, flash loans are limited by a token’s available liquidity. Flash swaps, however, are only constrained by storage limits, theoretically up to 1e128 tokens, far exceeding any token’s actual liquidity.

There’s no legitimate reason to “borrow” more tokens than will ever exist. That’s either a mistake or an attack, and definitely not a valid use case. Our guardrails now prevent these impossible scenarios from occurring at the pool level.

Setting the New Standard

The November 3rd exploit taught the industry valuable lessons. Our response reinforces our commitment to learning from incidents, even those that don’t directly affect our latest version.

By acting preventively rather than reactively, we’re committed to setting a new standard for AMM security, one where robustness is built into the architecture, and threats are blocked before they exist. Security goes beyond smart contract architecture. In collaboration with Hypernative, new pools feature extended pause capabilities backed by 24/7 monitoring, enabling immediate response when threats emerge and moving beyond rigid immutability toward active protection

New Weighted and Stable pool factories (including Stable Surge pools) with enhanced security guardrails are now deployed across all V3 networks. Learn more about Balancer V3 in our documentation.

Balancer x Certora: Future-Proofing Protocol Security was originally published in Balancer Protocol on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: Balancer V3: Why It Is Here To Stay
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Introduction

On November 3rd, an exploit drained $121M from V2 Composable Stable Pools across multiple chains. Balancer service providers published a full post-mortem with complete incident details. In response, V2’s footprint has been minimized, and BIP-887 got approved, marking V3 as the only Balancer platform for new liquidity, since standard Balancer V2 pool factories that can be disabled are being disabled. While existing V2 pools remain operational, Balancer service providers strongly encourage migration to V3.

The exploit was painful. But V3 wasn’t built to patch it. V3 launched before November 3rd. V3 was built to position Balancer for the next era of DeFi, keeping up with ecosystem advances while getting ahead of emerging threats.

Why V3 Was Built

V3 represents a complete rewrite driven by market evolution, technological advances, and lessons learned from V2’s operation.

The decision to build V3 came after the Linear Pool vulnerability, when the team faced a choice: patch V2 incrementally, or build something new. The conclusion was clear: merely patching wouldn’t be legitimate. V3 needed to deliver genuine advances beyond security fixes.

The Market

Ethereum’s transition to Proof-of-Stake changed DeFi’s economics. Liquid staking tokens and yield-bearing assets became dominant. The market demanded native support for these assets, not workarounds, but fundamental architecture designed around them.

V3’s buffer system enables gas-efficient integration with ERC-4626 vaults. Liquidity earns from both swap fees and underlying yield strategies simultaneously. No complex nesting, no additional gas overhead, just direct integration at the protocol level.

The Technology

Solidity advanced significantly since V2’s development. Two major language features made V3 possible:

Custom Errors (Solidity 0.7 → 0.8): V2 relied on cryptic error codes that required assembly workarounds. V3 uses native custom errors, cleaner code, better gas efficiency, improved developer experience.

Transient Storage (EIP-1153, Dencun upgrade): TLOAD/TSTORE opcodes reduced gas costs from thousands (SSTORE/SLOAD) to ~100. This enabled the “till pattern”, users perform complex operations within a callback, and the vault validates everything settled at the end. No separate relayer contracts needed.

Developer Experience

V2’s assumption proved wrong: that developers could build custom pools by just “tweaking at the bottom” while base contracts handled the complexity.

Reality: Any real custom pool needed to modify base-level logic: scaling, rates, fees, rounding. The barrier was too high. Few custom pools were built.

V3’s solution: move ALL complexity from pools to the vault.

Pools now implement three functions:

  • onSwap (calculation logic)
  • computeInvariant (pool invariant)
  • computeBalance (operation balances)

The vault handles token accounting, rate provider storage, decimal scaling, proper rounding, and fee calculations.

Concentrated Liquidity on V3

Market demand for concentrated liquidity was clear, but not everyone needed to solve it the same way.

V3’s approach: automatic concentrated liquidity through reCLAMM. Fungible positions instead of NFTs. Self-adjusting parameters for automatic rebalancing. Capital efficiency without constant manual management.

Security

The Linear Pool vulnerability taught critical lessons about rounding, reentrancy, and the need for protocol-level guardrails. V3 incorporated these lessons, and now, new lessons from the CSPv6 exploit:

  • BPT-aware vault with centralized accounting to prevent reentrancy
  • Renewed focus on correct rounding in every operation
  • Guardrails against unknown threats: minimum supply, minimum swap amounts, minimum fees

V3’s philosophy: we’re not just addressing today’s threat landscape. We’re building for threats that might emerge years from now.

The Result

V3 delivers:

Capital Efficiency: Native yield-bearing token support through buffer system integration.

Enhanced Programmability: Hooks enable extending pool behavior, dynamic fees, custom rebalancing logic, MEV reduction, without the overhead of creating entirely new pool types. New pool types require UI integration, subgraph indexing, monitoring setup, and aggregator adoption. Hooks attach to existing pool types that already have this infrastructure.

Infrastructure Improvements: Permissionless routers separate user interface from core accounting. Standard Router, Batch Router, Buffer Router, Composite Liquidity Router, each optimized for specific use cases, all updatable without touching security-critical vault code.

Developer Experience: Pools implement the invariant. The vault handles everything else.

And on top of these advances, V3’s architecture eliminates the vulnerability that enabled the November 3rd exploit.

Why V3 Would Avoid This Exploit

The fundamental reason V3 is safe: V3 doesn’t have the rounding error that V2 had.

All known exploits require some kind of error to manipulate. V2’s vulnerability was in “amount in” rounding. The November 3rd attack exploited a rounding error in the swap path, combined with rate providers supplying imprecision that amplified the error.

V3 addressed this through rigorous rounding direction implementation at the architectural level.

Vault-Centric Rounding

V2’s approach left rounding logic distributed across pools. Different pools handled rounding differently. Edge cases went untested.

V3 consolidates rounding into the vault. The vault knows the operation context (add liquidity, remove, swap) and tells the pool which direction to round.

Two functions:

  • invariant_up - round up when operation requires conservative rounding
  • invariant_down - round down when operation allows

The vault calls the appropriate version based on operation type. Pools receive explicit instructions.

V3’s Additional Prevention Mechanisms

Beyond fixing the fundamental rounding error, V3 implements multiple prevention layers:

No ExitSwaps: V2 allowed draining pools to very low liquidity states through exitSwaps. V3 makes BPT non-transient in batch swaps, blocking this attack path.

Centralized Accounting: V2’s distributed state, token balances in the vault, BPT logic in pools, created synchronization risk. V3’s vault implements a partial ERC-1155 implementation (the ERC20MultiToken pattern), handling all pool tokens and all minting/burning directly. State atomicity by design. No window where the vault’s view differs from the pool’s view.

Transient Storage: Balance deltas live in transient storage during execution. The vault validates everything nets to zero before committing. Either all operations succeed with valid final state, or the transaction reverts. Attackers can’t exploit intermediate states because intermediate states never touch persistent storage.

Migration

BIP-887 marks V3 as the only Balancer platform for new liquidity. Standard Balancer V2 pool factories that can be disabled are being disabled for better resource allocation. Rather than patching V2 indefinitely, resources are being channeled toward V3’s evolution.

What This Means

For LPs: V3 offers better security, improved capital efficiency through native yield-bearing token support, and more strategies through the hooks system. Migration isn’t mandatory, V2 pools still function. But Balancer service providers strongly recommend migration for enhanced security and support.

For Protocols: V3’s simplified development model and vault-centric architecture make custom AMM strategies more accessible. Hooks provide extensibility without the overhead of creating new pool types, no UI integration, subgraph indexing, monitoring setup, and aggregator adoption required. Hooks attach to existing pool types that already have this infrastructure. (Note: hooks still require some integration work, registration for UI display, but less than new pool types.)

Conclusion

Balancer’s mission is to be the programmable liquidity layer for DeFi. V2 advanced that mission. V3 continues it, built not as a patch, but as evolution.

V3 represents keeping up with advances: language features, ecosystem patterns, market demands. And getting ahead of threats: not just fixing yesterday’s vulnerabilities, but architecting against tomorrow’s unknowns.

The November 3rd exploit reinforced what V3 already demonstrated: fundamental architectural choices matter more than incremental patches. V3 eliminated the rounding error at its core, implemented rigorous testing impossible in V2, and built in guardrails against threats we haven’t seen yet.

Balancer V3 is live across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Gnosis, Avalanche, and zkEVM. Learn more at balancer.fi or connect with the team in Discord.

item.title: Nov 3 Exploit Post-Mortem
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Introduction

On November 3, 2025, at 7:46 AM UTC, Balancer V2 suffered an exploit affecting Composable Stable Pools. The exploit resulted in an estimated $94.8M theft of user funds. The chart below presents a summary of the exploit and recovered funds.

Thanks to rapid response from security partners, emergency interventions by blockchain foundations, whitehat rescuers operating under the SEAL Safe Harbor Agreement, and coordinated ecosystem response, funds were protected or recovered, and the impact of the theft was substantially mitigated.

The theft primarily affected V5 Composable Stable Pools (CSPv5) on V2, which are a specific subset of legacy Balancer V2 pools. Most of the Balancer protocol was unaffected by this exploit: notably V3, which has a completely different architecture and codebase.

On V2, all variants of Weighted Pools, Gyro Pools, and other types of Stable Pools were unaffected by this exploit. Vulnerable V6 Composable Stable Pools (CSPv6) were still within their pause windows. These were all paused within minutes of detection, blocking further exploits and enabling successful withdrawals by LPs (e.g., Crypto.com, Ether.fi).

This post-mortem covers only Balancer-deployed pools and the information Balancer currently has and is able to share. The Balancer community and service providers (”Balancer”) cannot comment on the security posture or recovery efforts of protocol forks, as Balancer does not have operational control over them.

Technical Breakdown

The Core Exploit: Rounding Direction

The exploit was ultimately enabled by incorrect rounding in the “exact out” swap path for Stable Pools. This type of swap allows users to specify the exact amount of tokens they want to receive (amountOut), with the smart contract calculating the required input amount (amountIn).

In _swapGivenOut, the amountOut is adjusted for the token decimals and rate, then rounded down by _upscale before being passed into the calculation. While this is not obvious at first glance (outputs are usually rounded down, after all), StableMath’s mechanics cause the amountIn to be rounded down as well. This produces an amountIn that is too low, causing the caller to underpay for the given amountOut.

Exploitation Mechanism

This exploit required three preconditions: 1) the underlying rounding error in exact out swaps; 2) rate providers, to introduce imprecision in the math; and 3) a low liquidity state, required to magnify the imprecision enough to be exploitable.

Only Composable Stable Pools satisfied all three conditions: and only if they actually incorporated BPT and rate providers. (A few were not using yield tokens or composability features, and were therefore not vulnerable.)

The V2 Vault enforces a strict separation between swaps and liquidity operations (called joins and exits in V2). Since the Vault is non-reentrant, there is no native way to do a join or exit and a swap in the same transaction, which limited the range of use cases.

Composable pools solved this problem by adding the pool’s own BPT as a token. Then BPT could be swapped in (joinSwap) or out (exitSwap) in a regular batch swap operation. The batch mechanism enabled flash swaps; i.e., “borrowing” virtual tokens in any amount, as long as the credits and debits balanced out during settlement.

This combination of features allowed “exitSwaps”: i.e., burning BPT that the caller didn’t actually have, and enabled putting the pool into a low liquidity state, which in combination with the error and imprecision made CSPs exploitable.

In the exploit, the attacker first drained the pool with an exitSwap. In these low liquidity conditions, the rounding error in the swap path could be magnified. Then came a long series of swaps, with amounts carefully calculated to generate the maximum loss from rounding. This progressively lowered the invariant (and therefore the value of the BPT), so that large balances of value tokens remained after repaying the BPT “flash swap” loan.

Fund Extraction Pattern

In many instances, the exploited funds did not immediately leave the Balancer Vault. Instead, they accumulated as “internal balance” — funds credited to the attacker’s account within the Vault’s internal accounting system but not yet withdrawn to an external wallet. The attackers then executed separate withdrawal transactions to extract these accumulated internal balances to addresses under their control.

The internal balance feature itself did not contribute to the vulnerability.

For readers interested in a deep technical analysis, both Certora and Trail of Bits have published comprehensive breakdowns of the incident. These reports have the most current understanding of the attack vectors:

  • Certora: Breaking Down the Balancer Hack
  • Trail of Bits: Balancer Hack Analysis and Guidance for the DeFi Ecosystem

Why Other Pool Types Were Not Vulnerable

Standard V2 Stable Pools do not have rate providers, so they only satisfy one of the conditions listed above. MetaStable Pools have rate providers, but do not satisfy the third condition (low liquidity), so they could not be exploited by this particular attack.

Weighted Pools do not have rate providers, and also use completely different math, where power functions are used to compute the invariant. The weighted swap functions are designed to compensate for the much greater maximum error inherent in these functions, ensuring that any single-wei rounding errors in previous steps are swamped by that adjustment.

Gyro Pools also use very different math, and additionally incorporate virtual balances, so that small deltas in “real” token balances do not affect the overall result.

Timeline

The response to this incident demonstrated the effectiveness of layered security architecture. The timeline of major events on November 3, 2025, is as follows:

07:46 UTC — First malicious transactions detected nearly simultaneously across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and Polygon

07:46 UTC — Bitfinding successfully front-ran attacker on Ethereum Mainnet, recovering ~$964k in WETH, wstETH, weETH, rETH, and osETH

07:52 UTC — Hypernative’s security monitoring systems flagged the suspicious activity and established emergency communication with Balancer’s operations team. A war room was created to coordinate the response.

08:07 UTC — V6 Composable Stable Pool implementations paused across affected networks, immediately protecting $19.3M in liquidity

08:14 UTC — SEAL 911 proactively contacted Balancer, having independently flagged attacker wallets in their systems

08:29 UTC — Teams completed identification and flagging of all attacker addresses across affected chains, enabling downstream security measures by exchanges and other protocols

09:50 UTC — First public disclosure made via Balancer’s official X/Twitter account, warning users of the ongoing incident while avoiding technical details that could enable copycat attacks

11:01 UTC — Recovery Mode activated on affected pools, enabling users to safely withdraw remaining funds through a simplified proportional exit mechanism

Financial Impact

The theft resulted in $121.1M in total losses across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and Polygon. Affected assets included various forms of staked and wrapped ETH (WETH, osETH, wstETH, frxETH, rsETH, rETH), osGNO, and other tokens. A list of affected pools can be found here [PLACEHOLDER: link].

However, thanks to a coordinated response from security partners, emergency intervention by blockchain foundations, and whitehat rescuers operating under the SEAL Safe Harbor Agreement, a significant amount of funds was protected or recovered. Recovery and mitigation efforts began within minutes of detection.

Recovery Summary

Thanks to coordinated response efforts, approximately $45.7M in user funds were protected or recovered through multiple security measures deployed promptly after detection.

Emergency Response Actions

V6 Pool Pauses

Protected $19.3M in vulnerable liquidity. Major LPs (Crypto.com, Ether.fi) withdrew safely.

Other Interventions

Gnosis implemented zero daily bridge limits on top tokens, freezing cross-chain movement of stolen funds.

Whitehat Recoveries (SEAL Safe Harbor Framework)

Total whitehat recoveries totaled $4.6M across multiple chains.

  • Ethereum (Bitfinding) — ~$964k recovered. 136.0 WETH, 11.0 wstETH, 6.6 weETH, 6.2 rETH, 105.2 osETH
  • Polygon (Safe Harbor whitehat) — ~$2.68M recovered. 6.8M MaticX, 8.0M WPOL, 72k stMatic, 2.9M TruMATIC
  • Base (Safe Harbor whitehat) — ~$161k recovered. 17.0 WETH, 24.2 rETH, 0.1 weETH
  • Arbitrum (anon whitehat) — ~$49k recovered. 13.8 ETH, various stablecoins and LSTs — already returned to DAO multisig

StakeWise DAO Emergency Operation

StakeWise DAO executed emergency recovery 90 minutes after the initial exploit using their multisig governance:

  • 5,041 osETH recovered — ~$19M (73.5% of stolen osETH)
  • 13,496 osGNO recovered — ~$1.9M (100% of stolen osGNO)

StakeWise is managing distribution directly to their users through their own governance process.

Impact Summary

Funds Lost to Attacker: $121.1.8M

Funds Protected (Mitigation): ~$19.3M

  • Emergency CSPv6 pools paused: $19.3M

Funds Recovered: ~$21.5M

  • Whitehat rescues (SEAL framework): $4.6M
  • StakeWise DAO emergency operation: $21.8M
  • Other interventions: Gnosis & Monerium

Secured Through Coordinated Response: ~$45.7M

Security Responses

This attack proves the value of Balancer’s layered security architecture:

  • Real-time monitoring: Hypernative’s systems promptly detected the attack, enabling rapid response and significantly reducing potential losses
  • Flash audits by security partners: Certora and Trail of Bits joined the war room and conducted immediate re-audits following the incident, identifying the MetaStable pool vulnerability and enabling preventive whitehat operations before attackers could discover this vector
  • Ecosystem responses: Gnosis Foundation implemented bridge limits, preventing cross-chain movement of stolen funds. Protocol partners including Beefy Finance, Aura Finance, and others responded quickly to assess exposure and protect users
  • Emergency pause capabilities: CSPv6 pools were paused, protecting $19.4M in vulnerable liquidity
  • SEAL Safe Harbor Agreement: Provided the legal framework enabling whitehat researchers to intervene decisively, with multiple successful front-running operations recovering funds
  • A new value extraction path was identified in V2 meta-stable pools. In coordination with Certora, SEAL911 and Balancer teams initiated a whitehat recovery, and have transferred ~$4.1M to controlled custody for reconciliation and return. See this X post for more information

Why Balancer V3 Is Unaffected

Balancer V3 was completely unaffected by this attack. While V3 was designed before this vulnerability was discovered, its architectural principles proved effective in preventing attacks of this nature.

V3’s design prioritized simplification and explicit controls. Calculations use consistent 18-decimal precision, with upscaling and downscaling handled by the Vault rather than individual pools. This reduces both mathematical complexity and potential attack surface.

Balancer V3 also implements explicit rounding controls: every arithmetic operation has an enforced rounding direction. V3 development employed rigorous formal verification, including properties for roundtrip swap invariance and BPT share value invariants.

The incident validates the value of building protocols with security-first architectural principles, even when specific attack vectors are not yet known. Both Certora and Trail of Bits have published detailed analyses explaining V3’s security architecture, and why it’s an improvement over V2 in terms of safety and eliminating possible attack vectors.

V2 Stable Pool Sunsetting

The transition away from V2 has been ongoing since the launch of V3 last December, and this event has prompted an acceleration of those plans (see the next section for details).

Balancer strongly encourages liquidity providers in stable pools to migrate to Balancer V3, which offers an enhanced security architecture and improved features. Detailed migration guidance, including timeline and incentive programs, will be shared in the near future.

V2 to V3 Transition Plan

On November 4, the Emergency SubDAO killed all gauges associated with affected V2 pools, stopping BAL incentive distributions to exploited pools. On November 5, CSPv6 factory contracts were disabled across all chains, preventing the creation of any new Composable Stable Pools.

With these measures in place, Balancer is working with ecosystem partners to facilitate a smooth migration path for liquidity providers from V2 stable pools to Balancer V3. Balancer has doubled down with partners on securing V2 pools and migrating them to the equivalent V3 pools. Here’s what’s relevant for V2 pool LPs:

  • For Weighted Pool LPs: Your pools remain fully operational and unaffected. No immediate action is required. In particular, the BAL/WETH Pool, BAL minting, veBAL, and the LM architecture must and will remain on V2.
  • For Gyro Pool LPs: Your pools remain fully operational and unaffected. New LPs are encouraged to use V3 Gyro pools, but no migration is required.
  • For V2 Stable Pool LPs: Balancer strongly encourages migrating to V3 stable pools. A comprehensive migration proposal with detailed guidance, timelines, and incentive programs will be shared separately. More information on migration timelines will be provided in the coming days.

For more information on the V2 to V3 transition, check the relevant forum post and ongoing governance proposal here.

Recovery Path for Affected LPs

Balancer is committed to be transparent as possible about how recovered funds may be returned. Since the recovered assets are now controlled by the DAO multisig, a proposal needs to be brought forward for veBAL governance to decide how to proceed. Our intent is not to socialize the loss, but rather to return the funds on a pool-by-pool basis.

  • For pools with recovered funds: If your pool had funds recovered through whitehat operations, Balancer will propose that those funds be returned to LPs of that specific pool proportional to their positions at the time of the exploit.
  • For pools without recovery: If your pool’s funds have not been recovered at this time, each pool’s recovery is handled independently. However, Balancer is committed to pursuing all available recovery efforts through law enforcement coordination, exchange cooperation, and other legal avenues. Balancer will continue to update those affected on these ongoing efforts.

Balancer is planning to coordinate with service providers to facilitate the claiming process for recovered funds. LPs will need to actively claim their recovered funds, rather than receiving automatic airdrops. This approach prevents sending funds to inactive wallets or addresses where keys may have been lost, and ensures that funds go to addresses that can actually access them. More information about the claiming process will be shared on a future governance proposal (BIP) soon.

Important notes on self custody:

  • StakeWise DAO is managing the distribution of recovered osGNO and osETH directly to their users. These funds are in StakeWise’s custody, not Balancer’s, and will be handled according to their own governance processes.
  • Assets frozen by blockchain ecosystems (such as on Gnosis Chain) remain in those entity’s custody. Balancer will provide updates as coordination with these foundations progresses and return processes are established.

The above applies to currently recovered funds. We remain committed to continuing recovery efforts through law enforcement coordination and all available legal channels.

Initial Learnings

This incident showed that security must be continuous. Even long-running, audited contracts need fresh reviews as new attack vectors and techniques emerge. Regular re-audits and deeper testing are essential to keep pace with how quickly threats evolve.

It also proved the value of strong security partnerships. The SEAL Safe Harbor framework enabled whitehats to act quickly and legally, helping to recover a meaningful amount of funds, and showing how coordinated ecosystem responses strengthen overall security.

Looking Ahead

Balancer regrets that its users experienced losses. However, this theft has also demonstrated significant strengths. Within minutes of detection, security partners, Balancer SPs, and the broader ecosystem mobilized to contain the damage. Through whitehat rescues, the StakeWise emergency recovery operation, foundation asset freezes, network-level interventions, and proactive threat hunting, Balancer protected or recovered significant funds.

Balancer remains committed to transparent communication throughout the recovery process, supporting law enforcement efforts to hold bad actors accountable, learning from this incident to strengthen security across the DeFi ecosystem, returning recovered funds to affected users, and building the future of decentralized exchange on Balancer V3’s secure foundation.

To liquidity providers whose funds were not recovered, we understand the frustration and uncertainty you are experiencing. While some pools did not have successful whitehat recovery operations, please know that our commitment to recovering your funds has not ended. Our legal team is actively working with law enforcement agencies across multiple jurisdictions, coordinating with other ecosystem players to monitor and freeze stolen assets, and pursuing every available legal avenue. These investigations take time, but they remain a top priority.

As the investigation progresses, Balancer will update those affected whenever practical with non-sensitive information through our official channels: X/Twitter (@Balancer), Discord, and Forum. Balancer will maintain dedicated support channels for affected LPs throughout the recovery process, and provide technical documentation for the claiming process when it launches.

item.title: LBPs Are Back: We’re Bringing Back Fair Token Distribution.
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Intro

The Dutch auction mechanism that helped DeFi protocol to make fair token launches is back. After a quiet period, Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools (or LBPs) are back on Balancer, starting with Hyperwave’s upcoming token launch.

While other methods dominated the recent cycle, the LBP model is still the only that delivered fair launches and token distribution as of now.

How LBPs Work

LBPs are AMM pools where token weights change over time according to preset schedules. A typical configuration starts at 95/5 (project token/collateral) and moves to 50/50 or even 20/80 by the end. This weight shift mechanically reduces the token price over time. Buyers who wait generally get better prices than those who rush in early.

Early purchases happen at the highest prices with guaranteed downward pressure ahead. Patient participants can time their entries as price approaches fair value. Large buyers face massive slippage on top of the weight-induced price decline. This creates natural protection against whales without requiring wallet caps, lottery systems, or KYC verification.

Where other token launch mechanisms demanded 50% of target liquidity upfront, LBPs function with 5–10% of that amount. This capital efficiency advantage becomes crucial for teams that need to preserve treasury while still providing functional price discovery.

What Made LBPs Work (And Why They Went Quiet)

Between 2020 and 2022, Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools (or LBPs) established themselves as the anti-whale token launch mechanism. The process starts with heavily weighted pools (think 95% project token, 5% collateral), then shifts weights gradually toward equilibrium over 2–5 days. This creates continuous downward price pressure unless genuine demand exceeds the mechanical decline.

Radicle raised $24.73 million with record trading volume. HydraDX achieved 87% token distribution across thousands of participants despite $70 gas fees on Ethereum back then. Projects needed just 10–20% of the capital required for traditional launches.

But LBPs largely disappeared after 2022. Points-based airdrops dominated 2024, distributing over $4 billion in tokens, and CEXs launches offered the credibility for new projects and tokens, and then LBPs fell into the shadows.

The Airdrop Era

The 2023–2024 cycle elevated points-based airdrops to dominant status. The model promised fairness through merit-based rewards: users who genuinely engaged with protocols over months would receive proportional allocations based on tracked activity.

But airdrop launches revealed a pattern: projects tacitly allowed data manipulation to attract funding, only to conduct large-scale purges before distribution. This created “a ruthless competition driven purely by self-interest” where airdrop hunters faced the dilemma of “if you farm, you might not get anything, but if you don’t farm, you’ll definitely get nothing.”

LayerZero identified between 1.1 and 1.3 million Sybil wallets during their detection phase, meaning that fake accounts were created solely to play on game allocation formulas. zkSync’s June 2024 airdrop excluded nearly 90% of addresses that interacted with the blockchain, with only 695,000 wallets eligible despite millions of participants. Critics noted zkSync enforced “almost no Sybil filtering,” making it one of the most farmable and farmed airdrop ever.

The problem is: points systems are “centralized data that can be manipulated and non-transparent, inflated infinitely or rules adjusted arbitrarily, raising concerns about fairness.” When too many participants flocked to single airdrops, rewards spread thin. What promised fair community distribution instead rewarded industrial-scale farming operations using hundreds of wallets, while genuine users received minimal allocations.

LBPs operate differently. While airdrops rely on points calculations vulnerable to gaming, LBPs use transparent on-chain price discovery. In airdrop systems Sybil attackers can create unlimited wallets to multiply rewards, LBPs naturally punish large capital deployment through slippage. The Dutch auction structure makes early whale purchases economically irrational, the opposite of airdrop dynamics where whale farmers optimize for maximum extraction.

LBPs vs The Alternatives

Points-based airdrops reward protocol usage over months but delay token availability, create farming behavior rather than genuine usage, and often disappoint participants when conversion rates arrive below expectations.

How LBPs Work

LBPs are AMM pools where token weights change over time according to preset schedules. A typical configuration starts at 95/5 (project token/collateral) and moves to 50/50 or even 20/80 by the end. This weight shift mechanically reduces the token price over time. Buyers who wait generally get better prices than those who rush in early.

Early purchases happen at the highest prices with guaranteed downward pressure ahead. Patient participants can time their entries as price approaches fair value. Large buyers face massive slippage on top of the weight-induced price decline. This creates natural protection against whales without requiring wallet caps, lottery systems, or KYC verification.

Where other token launch mechanisms demanded 50% of target liquidity upfront, LBPs function with 5–10% of that amount. This capital efficiency advantage becomes crucial for teams that need to preserve treasury while still providing functional price discovery.

Centralized exchange launches deliver instant credibility but costs run from $250K to over $1M including listing fees, legal work, and market makers. The 3–6 month timeline and requirement for 100K+ communities creates barriers most projects can’t meet.

Standard IDO launchpads provide middle-ground options at $180K-$700K total cost but require launchpad token holdings and take 1–5% fee structures.

Direct DEX listings offer maximum speed but require huge capital commitment ($100K-$500K for reasonable depth on Ethereum) and provide no inherent price discovery. Early whales can dominate.

LBPs fit projects with moderate budgets, communities under 50K participants, and priorities around fair distribution and capital efficiency. The mechanism combines transparency, capital efficiency, and anti-whale protection without centralized gatekeepers.

The Comeback

Hyperwave’s October 16–20 launch on HyperEVM brings LBPs back into focus. The decision to use LBPs rather than points distribution or exchange listings signals intentionality around community-led fundraising. Hyperwave’s approach allows purchasers and Wave Points holders to receive unlocked allocations while team and foundation tokens vest over 12–36 months.

The return of LBPs on Balancer V3 opens questions about token distribution strategy heading into the next market phase. Will other projects follow Hyperwave’s lead? Does the capital efficiency argument resonate more strongly now than during the 2024 points meta

Market conditions favor mechanisms that enable fair distribution without centralized gatekeepers. Regulatory clarity emerging in the US, EU, and UK makes transparent on-chain launches more viable. Projects with genuine communities but moderate marketing budgets need capital-efficient options beyond either giving tokens away or paying six-figure exchange fees.

LBPs never stopped working. The market just needed to remember why they mattered.

LBPs Are Back: We’re Bringing Back Fair Token Distribution. was originally published in Balancer Protocol on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

Balancer Report — September 2025

The Balancer Report

Get the latest on ecosystem news, key metrics, governance proposals, and everything shaping what’s next. Stay ahead, let’s dive in!

Balancer Conquers Plasma.

September 2025 will be remembered as the month Balancer proved why it’s the premier liquidity infrastructure for stablecoins. Balancer v3 launched on Plasma and achieved $200M TVL in just one week, proving the demand for deep stablecoin liquidity.

Plasma is an EVM chain purpose-built for stablecoins, featuring zero-fee USDT transfers and sub-second finality. When the blockchain designed for stable assets meets the AMM perfected for stable pairs, the results speak for themselves.

Why Plasma Chose Balancer

This partnership didn’t happen by accident. Plasma invited Balancer to be part of its foundation, with strong encouragement from Aave. The synergy is clear: wherever Aave deploys, Balancer provides the critical liquidity layer. This positions both protocols to anchor Plasma’s liquidity stack from day one.

The strategic advantages:

  • Early entry before competing AMMs gain traction
  • Demonstration of v3’s unique capabilities in boosted stable pools, reCLAMM, and flexible design
  • Strong backing from Aave for Boosted pool liquidity
  • Phased approach with measurable milestones for sustainable growth

You can dive deeper into the Balancer <> Plasma synergy here!

Flagship Pools Driving Adoption

USDe/USDT0

Ethena Labs’ USDe it’s a synthetic dollar backed by crypto collateral with delta-hedging strategies. No bank dependencies.

The USDe/USDT pool showcases the full power of Balancer v3:

  • Boosted Pool technology: 100% of liquidity deployed to Aave lending markets while maintaining instant swap execution
  • StableSurge hook: Dynamic fees that automatically increase on unbalancing trades and decrease for balanced flow
  • Triple yield streams: Swap fees + Aave lending yields + optimal capital efficiency

This pool reached $28M TVL by combining stable pool mechanics with intelligent fee optimization and maximum capital utilization. Every dollar works overtime.

WXPL/USDT0 reCLAMM pool

Traditional concentrated liquidity pools have a problem: when price moves outside your range, your liquidity goes dormant. You wake up to “out of range” positions. Manual rebalancing required. Opportunities missed.

reCLAMM pools change everything.

The WXPL/USDT0 pool is processing $9.9M daily volume with just $3.8M average TVL, that’s a 260% volume-to-TVL ratio, or 2.6x turnover on a daily basis. This level of capital efficiency makes traditional AMMs look obsolete by comparison.

What makes reCLAMM revolutionary:

  • Automatic parameter adjustment based on trading activity
  • Oracle-free operation — pure on-chain logic, no external keeper dependencies
  • No price feed manipulation risk — market-driven adjustments only
  • Continuously active liquidity — no manual rebalancing required

Building on Plasma’s infrastructure (sub-second finality + low fees) combined with reCLAMM automation creates the optimal environment for concentrated liquidity. Set it and forget it. Your liquidity stays active while the automated parameters handle market volatility.

Additional Launch Pools:

The Plasma deployment included a comprehensive suite of pools designed to establish Balancer as the liquidity foundation:

  • USDai / USDT
  • sUSDe / USDT
  • WETH / weETH
  • xUSD / USDT
  • WETH / wrsETH
  • sUSDai / USDT
  • WXPL / USDT

Latest Ecosystem News

Stream Protocol Partnership

Stream Protocol specializes in capital-efficient vaults with delta-neutral strategies delivering 8–18% APY and zero directional risk exposure. They chose Balancer v3 as their liquidity foundation, and the partnership makes perfect strategic sense.

Four pools now live across multiple chains:

  1. xUSD/USDT on Plasma — The flagship pool bringing Stream’s vault tokens to the stablecoin hub
  2. USDC/xUSD on Arbitrum — Expanding Stream’s reach to Arbitrum’s DeFi ecosystem
  3. mevUSDC/xUSD on Avalanche — Capital-efficient vault liquidity on Avalanche
  4. BTC.b/xBTC on Avalanche — Breaking into BTC-correlated strategies

Treehouse + Balancer Enhances Avalanche LST Ecosystem

AVAX liquidity providers now have access to a turbocharged liquid staking solution through Treehouse’s partnership with Balancer v3.

The tAVAX/sAVAX Boosted Pool on Aave combines:

  • sAVAX (Benqi Staked AVAX): Your staked AVAX continues earning validation rewards while remaining tradeable across DeFi. No lockups, no compromise, pure capital efficiency.
  • tAVAX (Treehouse yield-optimized LST): Doesn’t just collect staking rewards — it deploys advanced strategies including arbitrage opportunities to amplify returns beyond standard staking APY.

What makes this pool unstoppable:

Pairing these two liquid staking tokens in a v3 Boosted Pool creates the ultimate staking hub:

  • Both tokens earning their respective yield strategies
  • Swap fees from arbitrage flow between the tokens
  • Treehouse Avalanche Ascent point multipliers for active participation
  • StableSurge hook protection ensuring LPs capture maximum value during volatile periods

The traditional trade-off eliminated:

Traditional staking = locked liquidity with no DeFi access Other DEXs = trading fees only, no staking rewards Balancer v3 + Treehouse = simultaneous fee collection, staking rewards, AND bonus point accumulation

The Avalanche Ascent program brings a gamified approach to liquid staking, rewarding active participation across DeFi with Balancer pools serving as core infrastructure for tAVAX/sAVAX liquidity and trading.

Rezerve Weighted Pools

Rezerve just pioneered a new category of treasury protocols by deploying their accumulation strategy on Balancer V3. Their ambitious mission: accumulate 1M ETH through pure DeFi mechanics.

Rezerve’s Revolutionary Approach:

  • Harberger Tax Revenue: Predictable income stream from declared asset values without requiring token sales
  • Compounding Bonds: Auto-restaking over 4-day cycles that capture every epoch for maximum efficiency
  • Multi-tier Defense System: Comprehensive protection from reward throttling to insurance mechanisms

Why Balancer V3 as the Liquidity Foundation:

Rezerve chose Balancer after evaluating the entire DeFi landscape. The decision came down to three critical factors:

  1. Vault Architecture: Perfect for complex treasury management operations requiring sophisticated asset coordination
  2. Capital Efficiency: Maximum utilization of protocol-controlled assets through 80/20 RZR weighted pools that maintain liquidity while reducing impermanent loss
  3. Programmable Liquidity: The flexibility to architect an entire treasury management system using Balancer’s infrastructure as the foundation

This is what building on Balancer looks like in practice. Rezerve didn’t just use pools — they architected an entire treasury management system leveraging Balancer’s programmable liquidity infrastructure. The best protocols choose smart liquidity layers.

The 80/20 weighted pools allow Rezerve to maintain deep RZR liquidity while keeping the majority of their treasury in ETH, perfectly aligned with their accumulation strategy. Every mechanism designed to compound their path toward 1M ETH.

veBAL Stats — Defilytica

As of October 1st, 2025, veBAL was valued at $4.93, with a voting APR of 28.38%. This APR shows what veBAL holders can earn by locking BAL/WETH 80/20 BPT into the protocol.

This metric highlights veBAL’s role as more than just a governance tool — it’s designed to encourage active involvement in the protocol. The APR reflects the value of long-term participation, aligning economic incentives with decision-making power.

See details: Balancer Analytics

Governance Updates

Balancer’s Snapshot has activity with two proposals. Take a moment to read through them:

[BIP-872] Enable FYNI/waBasUSDC 70/30 Pool Gauge on Balancer v3 (Base) with a 2% Cap

This proposal seeks to add gauge support for the FYNI/waBasUSDC 70/30 weighted pool on Balancer v3 for Base network, with a 2% emissions cap to support liquidity growth for the FYNI token ecosystem.

[BIP-871] Balancer <-> QuantAMM Protocol Fee Framework

This proposal established the protocol fee agreement between Balancer DAO and the QuantAMM Team, clarifying the revenue split structure for Blockchain Traded Funds (BTFs) on Balancer V3.

Key Terms:

  • When a veBAL gauge is utilized and the pool qualifies as a core pool: 70% of protocol revenue recycled as bribes, 15% to QuantAMM, 15% to Balancer
  • When a pool has a gauge but is not a core pool: 50% QuantAMM, 50% Balancer
  • When no veBAL gauge is utilized: 80% to QuantAMM, 20% to Balancer DAO

The fee framework was designed to be equitable and align incentives between both protocols, strengthening the long-term relationship. The terms will be reviewed 18 months after QuantAMM’s launch (launch May 2025, review November 2026).

Be Careful What URLs You Visit!

🚨 THE LAUNCH OF ANY NEW UPDATE, VERSION, OR PRODUCT CAN ATTRACT SCAMMERS. WITH THE V3 LAUNCH AND PLASMA DEPLOYMENT, STAY EXTRA VIGILANT! 🚨

To avoid risk, bookmark the official URL balancer.fi and use the bookmark shortcut instead.

item.title: How Balancer is the Exact AMM for Stable Pairs That Plasma Needs
item.dc:creator: Joao
item.content:encoded:
Plasma launched its mainnet on September 25, 2025, capturing $5.6 billion in TVL within 96 hours. Backed by Tether, Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund, and Framework Ventures with over $400 million raised, Plasma offers zero-fee USDT transfers and sub-second finality.

The thesis: $250 billion stablecoin economy has grown large enough to justify dedicated infrastructure. This specialization creates opportunities for DeFi protocols that match this focus with equally optimized technology.

The Stablecoin Liquidity Problem

Stablecoin swaps present a challenge for traditional AMMs. Unlike volatile assets, stablecoins trade near parity. A USDT/USDC swap should execute with minimal slippage, but constant product formulas (x*y=k) fail this requirement.

Standard AMMs spread liquidity across the entire price curve, leaving capital idle at price points that will never be reached. The result: poor capital efficiency and unnecessary slippage.

Three requirements for stablecoin liquidity:

  • Maximum liquidity in the narrow range where stablecoins actually trade
  • Large swaps execute near parity without moving the market
  • Idle capital earns returns rather than sitting unused

Balancer’s Technical Stack for Stable Assets

Balancer V3 addresses these challenges through three complementary technologies.

Stable Pools implement StableSwap math optimized for assets trading near parity. The invariant concentrates capital in the narrow band where stablecoins actually trade, delivering dramatically better execution. The amplification parameter controls liquidity concentration, letting pool creators optimize for specific asset pairs.

Boosted Pools deploy 100% of liquidity on lending markets to generate yield while maintaining full swap functionality. Instead of leaving USDT unused, Boosted Pools deposit it into Aave and other lending markets. When swaps occur, the pool automatically withdraws, executes the trade, and redeposits surplus capital.

Liquidity buffers keep small amounts of each token immediately available, providing swap execution speed comparable to standard pools while generating continuous yield.

StableSurge adds dynamic fee adjustment. Traditional pools charge static fees regardless of market conditions. StableSurge monitors pool balance and volatility, automatically increasing fees on transactions that move the pool away from equilibrium while keeping fees low for balanced flow.

Why This Stack Is Perfect for Plasma

Plasma’s architecture and Balancer’s technology align across multiple dimensions:

  • Capital Efficiency Matches Zero-Fee Design: The zero-fee USDT transfer model makes capital efficiency paramount. Boosted Pools that generate yield on 100% of deposited capital directly match Plasma’s efficiency-first philosophy.
  • Concentrated Liquidity for Payment Volume: If Plasma succeeds as the dominant stablecoin payment layer, volume will be immense but spread across many small transactions. Stable Pools’ narrow liquidity concentration provides excellent execution for these routine swaps.
  • Deep Aave Integration: Aave deployed on Plasma to serve stablecoin lending demand. Balancer’s Boosted Pools automatically route liquidity to Aave, creating a tight loop: liquidity provision funds lending markets which generate yield for LPs which attracts more liquidity.
  • Strategic Timing: Plasma launched with over 100 DeFi protocols, but liquidity infrastructure isn’t yet entrenched. Balancer’s technical advantages can establish dominant positions before competition solidifies.

Building the Stablecoin Liquidity Layer

Plasma’s leadership targets the $250 billion stablecoin economy with a vision of reaching trillion-dollar scale. If even a fraction of stablecoin economic activity settles on Plasma, liquidity requirements will dwarf current deployments.

Balancer’s hooks system enables ongoing innovation without protocol upgrades. New fee strategies and capital efficiency techniques can deploy while maintaining backward compatibility.

Plasma provides the settlement layer. Balancer provides the liquidity layer. Together, we form the foundation for digital dollar economies that can scale to serve billions of users and trillions in transaction volume.

item.title: How we made Stable LP tokens suitable for lending
item.dc:creator: Sergio Yuhjtman
item.content:encoded:
The StableSwap pool type introduced by Curve has gained widespread adoption over time due to its high capital efficiency. Balancer has a long-standing history of embracing this concept and building upon it. As of today, there are approximately $300 million in Stable Balancer Pool Tokens combined. Recently, we addressed and solved a notable open problem in DeFi related to stable pools.

Recognizing the value of Stable Balancer Pool Tokens, we identified their strong potential as collateral in lending protocols. To enable the composition of utility between these two types of DeFi protocols, it is necessary to price the pool-tokens precisely. For a pool with n constituent tokens, the price of the pool-token can be expressed as:

where S is its total supply, xᵢ is the balance of the i-th token and pᵢ the price of the i-th token expressed in the desired unit.

Unfortunately, we cannot use the pool’s internal prices for this purpose, since they are prone to manipulation during short periods. Therefore, the prices will be given by an external oracle. See this post by Felix Leupold for more context. Two important hacks were caused precisely by the use of internal pool prices to determine the price of the pool-token. The affected protocols were Value Defi in 2020 and Inverse Finance in 2022.

A stable pool is a constant function AMM (CF-AMM). By calling f its defining function and D the value of the function at a given time, the system of equations

determines the values x for the non-manipulated balances. Here k is some positive real number to be found. In short, this is because the partial derivatives of f express the pool’s internal spot prices. We are therefore looking for the balances that align these internal prices with those provided by the oracle.

A detailed explanation of this fact and all the other technical details of the solution can be found at Pricing StableSwap pools. Interestingly, this mathematical formulation also solves the problem of finding the optimal arbitrage swap against an ideal source of infinite liquidity, with prices given by the vector p.

The system of equations might look intimidating when written out explicitly. However, it can be solved efficiently within a smart contract. Let us briefly explain the method we used.

Surprisingly, the equation for the gradient becomes a linear system if we treat the product of the balances as a constant. This simplification is valid because it can be compensated by rescaling the variables, thereby exploiting the homogeneity of f. In this way, we obtain an expression for the unknowns xᵢ that depends on a single parameter. By plugging these values into the equation f(x)=D, we obtain a nonlinear equation for the remaining parameter, which can be solved using Newton’s method. There are some crucial subtleties concerning the location of the relevant root, the convexity of the function, and the starting point for Newton’s method iterations.

Balancer’s smart contract team has swiftly implemented and verified this solution.

Further thoughts: lower and upper prices

If we combine the prices from the oracle with the actual balances of the pool — taking the inner product, as above — we will typically obtain the true value of the pool. If a manipulation happens, this will return a larger value. This holds for any CF-AMM with convex f, as explained in Section 1.2 of the technical paper. Dividing by S, we obtain a quantity that may be called the upper price. Following the same idea, it is possible to form a lower price.

These quantities can be computed very efficiently for a wide variety of pools. We believe that lending protocols could take advantage of this method for computing the prices to save their users significant amounts of gas.

If you are interested in this topic, reach out to us!

Get the latest on ecosystem news, key metrics, governance proposals, and everything shaping what’s next. Stay ahead, let’s dive in!

Latest ecosystem news

HyperEVM Deployment: Balancer’s Strategic Expansion

Balancer successfully deployed on HyperEVM, capitalizing on one of crypto’s fastest-growing ecosystems. HyperEVM achieved remarkable growth since its February 2025 launch, reaching $2 billion in TVL within five months and securing the 9th position globally, yet lacked sophisticated AMM infrastructure to match its explosive growth.

The deployment features Balancer v3’s advanced capabilities including custom hooks, boosted pools, and flexible architecture, serving an ecosystem with 200,000–400,000 daily transactions and 15,000–20,000 daily active users. A key technical advantage is the planned HyperCore integration, providing atomic access to real-time pricing from Hyperliquid’s $1.6 trillion cumulative volume order books, eliminating oracle manipulation risks.

New HyperEVM Pool Highlights:

  • 20+ diverse pools across Boosted, Weighted, and Gyro E-CLP categories
  • Multiple stablecoin pairs with advanced yield-generating mechanics
  • Strategic partnerships with Felix, HyperLend, Hyperbeat, and ecosystem leaders

reCLAMMs: The Evolution of Automated Liquidity

In July reCLAMMs (Readjusting Concentrated Liquidity AMM), a breakthrough passive approach to concentrated liquidity management. This technology keeps liquidity centered around market price, enabling trades to meet real depth without active management.

How reCLAMMs Work:

  • Passive Management: Pool adjusts itself automatically following predefined parameters
  • Enhanced Security: Fungible BPTs instead of NFTs ensure composability and reduce oracle operation risks
  • Trader Benefits: Better execution through maintained liquidity concentration
  • LP Protection: Gradual adjustments protect against impermanent loss

This month, the COW/WETH reCLAMM pool on Base exemplified this technology’s potential, accounting for over 80% of $COW trading volume on Base and delivering optimal pricing for traders while maintaining exceptional capital efficiency.

Explore the COW/WETH reCLAMM pool here!

Balancer v3 Live on GeckoTerminal

GeckoTerminal Integration Balancer v3 pools are now fully integrated with GeckoTerminal, providing users with comprehensive tracking capabilities:

  • Real-time data for all V3 pools
  • Advanced charting with smooth navigation
  • Multi-network support covering Ethereum and Base deployments
  • Links: Ethereum | Base

Balancer: TVL and Stats — Defilytica

As of August 27th, veBAL was valued at $5.88, with a voting APR of 31.45%. This APR shows what veBAL holders can earn by locking BAL/WETH 80/20 BPT into the protocol.

This metric highlights veBAL’s role as more than just a governance tool — it’s designed to encourage active involvement in the protocol. The APR reflects the value of long-term participation, aligning economic incentives with decision-making power.

See details: Balancer Analytics

Governance Updates

August saw a lot of governance activity with five BIPs approved strengthening Balancer’s operational framework:

[BIP-863] Legal Structure for Treasury Operations

Approved creation of “Balancer Business” entity in British Virgin Islands under Balancer OpCo Limited, replacing current DAO multisig for protocol fee management. This structure reduces regulatory risks, improves efficiency, and provides clear revenue flows while maintaining DAO governance authority.

[BIP-864] RZR/wstETH 80/20 Gauge Enabled

New gauge approved for RZR/wstETH pool on Balancer v3 Ethereum, with Rezerve team seeding over $700k in liquidity to establish this as the primary RZR liquidity venue.

[BIP-865] Emergency subDAO Permissions

Granted missing emergency permissions for v3 pool factories across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Base, ensuring rapid response capabilities for security incidents.

[BIP-866] TREE/WETH 80/20 Pool Gauge

Enabled gauge with 5% cap for TREE/WETH pool on v3 Ethereum, supported by $1.5M+ in seeded liquidity from Treehouse team.

[BIP-867] Universal Gauge Management

Streamlined gauge operations by granting Maxi Omni multisig universal permissions for routine gauge maintenance, reducing operational friction while maintaining DAO oversight.

Community & Events

Livestreams

Office Hours Regular community sessions featuring ecosystem partners and the Balancer product team:

  • Hyperbeat Collab: Technical discussions on AMM optimization with Hyperbeat
  • Dev Focused: Sessions with Xeonus, Zekraken, and Pawel Rak on operations and analytics

Product & Ecosystem Updates

  • HyperEVM Super Live: Deep dive into new deployment featuring ecosystem partners (Hyperbloom, Hyperwave, Looping Collective, HypurrFi)
  • reCLAMMs Deep Dive: Technical sessions with Sergio Yuhjtman (Researcher), Juani (Smart Contracts Lead), and João Bruno (Smart Contract Developer)

Balancer participated in Latin America’s largest blockchain event (August 5–7, 2025) in Rio de Janeiro. Fabio from the product team delivered an inspiring presentation about Balancer’s role in DeFi’s evolution to compete with centralized venues, reaching over 15,000 participants across nearly 400 speakers and 200+ sessions.
